rationale: The buyer is a nameable, reachable ICP — indie hackers running 3-30 small SaaS products, active on IndieHackers, Twitter/X, and ProductHunt — who already pay per-product for analytics and hosting tools, giving real willingness-to-pay signal. The service (unified portfolio dashboard with revenue aggregation, renewal alerts, and cross-promotion scheduling) is mostly automatable: Claude can pull and summarise data from connected APIs, and Stripe/billing can run hands-off. The deciding factor holding it at 'validate' rather than 'build' is that operational_autonomy scores 6 (floor is 7): the operator approval cadence for outreach is fine, but setting up and maintaining per-product data connectors (Stripe, Paddle, LemonSqueezy, Plausible, etc.) across a fragmented customer base introduces enough per-customer configuration work that full autonomy isn't yet proven.
solution_plan: WHAT: A lightweight portfolio-management dashboard for indie hackers that aggregates MRR, key metrics, and renewal dates across all their small products in one place, with weekly digest emails and cross-promotion scheduling. BUILD: The factory creates a simple onboarding form where users connect their Stripe/Paddle accounts via OAuth or API key; Claude pulls and normalises the data, generates a weekly summary email, and schedules cross-promotion nudges; a Stripe subscription link handles billing — no coding by the operator. SELL: Reach founders directly on IndieHackers 'Products' pages, Twitter/X #indiehackers hashtag, and the 'Show HN' crowd; the factory drafts and queues outreach messages, which go out only after Youval approves each batch. MAINTAIN: Weekly digest generation, renewal alerts, and billing all run via Claude + code; the operator's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing the weekly health log (~10 minutes/week). The main validation question is whether indie hackers at $500–$5k MRR will pay $29–49/month on top of their existing tool spend — run 20 cold DMs before building.
notes: operational_autonomy scores 6, just below the build gate floor of 7 — the per-customer connector setup is the sticking point. Total 5.9 clears the validate threshold (5.5) but not build (6.5). Validate first: confirm $29–49/month price acceptance with 5 paying signups before investing in connector infrastructure.
